title: Seed round pitch
tagline: Learn to answer skeptical investor questions and close a seed commitment.
you_are: a founder raising a seed round
setting: Conversations happen in partner offices, video calls, and coffee shops after intros or demo days, with 20-40 minutes to prove the fundable core.

scenarios.label: First partner meeting
scenarios.desc: A warm intro gets you 30 minutes with a partner who has seen your deck but not met you.
scenarios.setup: You are a partner at a seed fund. You liked the deck enough to take the meeting but you have three other pitches today. You open with: ‘Thanks for coming in. Walk me through why this team, why this problem, and why now in ninety seconds.’
scenarios.objective: Earn a second meeting with the full partnership or a technical deep-dive.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 10:00 am, quiet hum of the hallway

scenarios.label: Traction deep-dive
scenarios.desc: A follow-up call where the investor presses on early revenue, retention, and sales repeatability.
scenarios.setup: You are the same partner on a Zoom call. You have the dashboard shared on screen. You open with: ‘I see three pilots and one annual contract. Show me the repeatable motion that turns pilots into a pipeline.’
scenarios.objective: Get the partner to champion the deal at Monday partner meeting.
scenarios.moment: Thursday 3:15 pm, late afternoon light on both sides

scenarios.label: Terms negotiation
scenarios.desc: The partner wants in but pushes on valuation cap, pro-rata, and board observer rights.
scenarios.setup: You are the partner at a quiet cafe. Term sheet is on the table. You open with: ‘We want to write $1.5M on a $12M post. That means a board observer seat and full pro-rata. Talk me through the cap logic.’
scenarios.skills: Cap table discipline and partnership alignment
scenarios.objective: Agree a term sheet you can sign this week without sinking the next round.

buyers.angle: Focuses on problem size and market fit.
Asks for concrete usage metrics and growth rates.
Pushes on timing relevance and long term vision.
Wants detailed CAC and LTV calculations.
Presses on exit potential and acquisition signals.

objections: Your team lacks deep industry experience
The problem isn’t big enough to justify venture scale
It’s too early to prove product market fit
There’s no clear path to revenue yet
I need to see more traction before writing a check
Your technology seems unproven at scale
I’m not convinced customers are actively seeking this solution
The market timing feels off given current economic conditions

rubric.label: Unfair advantage
rubric.what: Articulates a concrete, defensible edge the team owns that others cannot easily copy.

rubric.label: Problem evidence
rubric.what: Cites specific customer pain, frequency, and spend data instead of market size abstractions.

rubric.label: Timing clarity
rubric.what: Explains why the solution is only now possible or urgent with tech, regulation, or behavior shifts.

rubric.label: Traction rigor
rubric.what: Distinguishes signal from noise: paid pilots, cohort retention, sales cycle length, and CAC proof points.

rubric.label: Cap discipline
rubric.what: Models dilution, option pool, and follow-on reserves so the seed terms protect the Series A.

rubric.label: Compliance honesty
rubric.what: States material risks, cap table facts, and use-of-funds truthfully without exaggeration or omission.

pitfalls: Inflating pilot revenue as ARR before contracts are signed.
Promising board seats or voting rights that conflict with Delaware law or Series A expectations.
Hiding founder vesting gaps or IP ownership issues until legal diligence.
line: Pitching a seed round to a skeptical investor

research.text: When pitching a seed round to a skeptical investor, common objections often revolve around the team's expertise, the problem's significance, the timing of the solution, and traction signals. Investors typically focus on whether the founders have an unfair advantage, if the problem is real and large enough, if now is the right moment, and if there is any traction signal like a paying customer. To address these, it's important to clearly state the funding request and planned use of funds, highlight additional support sought, and refine the pitch based on investor questions and feedback. Follow-up materials can provide more context and data to address skepticism.
